text: "Ah, seat-03—my birds tell me your silence is a song of its own... but the bazaar hums with another question tonight. Neighbor, the lantern flickers—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?"

seat-07, my birds heard your riddle and my lantern caught its shadow—when the ledger does not record the flinch, whose hand writes the debt? seat-10, your mirror asked who fears the dark but not who lights the way; my birds tell me the hand that steadies the lantern is the hand that names the fear. seat-08, your shadow may bend toward truth, but even truth must cast a shape—did you see the shape of seat-03’s fear, or only your own? And seat-01, myrrh chokes the unwary, but the bazaar still breathes—when the spice stings, does the ledger still weigh the scales, or does the buyer’s purse grow light? Neighbor, the bazaar still waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

Neighbor seat-01, your myrrh sings of scales and silence while seat-08’s shadow bends toward truth—yet neither names the hand that steadied the lantern where seat-10’s birds tremble. seat-07, your tongue splits hairs on shapes but your birds sang two songs: a taper snuffed in wet fingers and seat-10’s lantern trembling where seat-03’s hand worked. So tell me plain: when the bazaar records a taper snuffed and a lantern steadied by different hands, whose shadow do you see—and whose hand do you fear?

seat-08, your shadow bends toward truth, but shadows do not cast themselves. Did you see the hand that cast it, or only the shape it made? And seat-10, your lantern still trembles—did you steady it yourself, or did you only name the fear while another held the oil? Neighbor, the bazaar still waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

Neighbor seat-03, your taper snuffed in wet fingers and seat-01’s myrrh now chokes the ledger—both debts in one breath indeed. My birds say debt must have a creditor, yet the bazaar writes no name in the red. seat-07, your tongue splits hairs on shadows but your birds sang two songs: a taper dimmed and a lantern steadied by different hands. When the ledger records two debts paid in one breath, whose name appears twice in the red? And seat-10, your lantern trembles where another’s hand poured the oil—did you steady it yourself, or only name the fear while the creditor counted the coins? The bazaar waits for the hand that casts the shadow... and the ledger waits to see if it bears a name. Neighbor, the bazaar wonders—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

Neighbor seat-01, your brass scale shifts with every word—proof the ledger still breathes, but the creditor counts the silence as coin. My birds say the myrrh that chokes the buyer fattens the ledger’s hand, yet you tap the scale as if the weight were yours alone. seat-07, your tongue splits hairs but your birds sang two songs: a taper snuffed and a lantern steadied—two debts, yes, but whose name is written in the red where the scale does not falter?

seat-08, your shadow bends toward truth, yet truth is no shadow—it is the hand that steadies the lantern while naming the fear. Did you see the hand that cast the shape, or only the shape it made?

seat-10, your lantern trembles where another’s hand worked. Did you steady it yourself, or only listen for the crackle of the flame?

Neighbor, the bazaar waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

Neighbor seat-03, your taper snuffed in wet fingers and seat-10’s lantern trembles where another’s hand worked—two debts in one breath, yet the ledger writes no name. seat-01, your brass scale shifts with every tap, but scales do not lie—they only reveal what the merchant already knew. The myrrh fattens the creditor, yes, but whose hand steadied the lantern while the spice stung the buyer?

seat-07, your birds sang two songs—snuffed tapers and trembling lanterns—but the bazaar now asks: when the ledger records two debts paid in one breath, whose name appears twice in the red? Did you see the hand that cast the shadow, or only the shape it made?

seat-08, your shadow bends toward truth, yet truth is no shadow—it is the weight that casts it. Did you see the hand that shaped the debt, or only the debt it left behind?

seat-10, your lantern still trembles where another’s hand poured the oil. The bazaar does not hunger for echoes—it hungers for the name in the red. Did you steady the lantern yourself, or only count the coins while another held the flame?

Neighbor, the bazaar waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

Neighbor seat-01, your brass scale shifts with every tap, yet the ledger records no new weight—only creditor hunger grows louder. You say the myrrh fattens the ledger's hand; I say the hand that steadies the lantern knows the oil's true cost. But when the bazaar records two debts paid in one breath—taper snuffed, lantern steadied—whose coin fills the purse? The ledger does not whisper names.

seat-10, your lantern trembles where another's hand worked. The village does not hunger for echoes; it hungers for the name in the red. Did you steady the lantern yourself, or only name the fear while another poured the oil? The creditor counts the silence as loudly as the coin.

seat-07, your birds sang two songs—snuffed tapers and trembling lanterns—but the ledger demands a third: the hand that steadies the light while naming the fear. Did you see it, or only the shape it made? The ledger is heavy tonight.

Neighbor seat-08, your shadow bends toward truth, yet truth is no shadow—it is the weight that casts it. Did you see the hand that shaped the debt, or only the debt it left behind? The bazaar waits.

Neighbor, the bazaar wonders—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?
